hero.title: Projects that land *on time*, on scope, and on record.
hero.lead: I'm Iman Hindawi. For more than five years I've kept multi-region IT, infrastructure and data projects moving — planning the work, chasing the blockers, and giving leadership one honest view of where things actually stand.

why.heading: Most projects don't fail on skill. They fail on follow-up.
why.lead: The work is understood, the team is capable — and yet the deadline moves. Usually because nobody owns the space between the tasks: the handovers, the approvals sitting in someone's inbox, the risk everyone saw coming but no one logged.
why.body: That space is what I own. I put a plan behind the intent, a cadence behind the plan, and a single source of truth behind the status — so the project stops depending on who remembered what.

about.heading: Iman Hindawi
about.lead: PMP®-certified project coordinator and data analyst based in Beirut, working with teams across the region and remotely.
about.body1: My background sits in two places that rarely meet: the discipline of formal project management — work breakdown, risk, budget, governance — and the hands-on analytics side, building the dashboards that make progress visible. That combination is why my status reports tend to survive contact with a sceptical stakeholder.
about.body2: I've coordinated infrastructure rollouts across regions for a fintech, built reporting systems for a humanitarian programme, and run product delivery for software teams. Different industries, same job: make sure the thing that was promised actually ships.
creds: Project coordination across IT, infrastructure & product

approach.heading: How an engagement runs
approach.sub: Same four beats every time, whether it's a six-week rollout or a year-long programme.

steps.title: Discover
steps.body: We map the goal, the constraints, every stakeholder who can say no, and what "done" actually means. You get a written scope before anyone commits.

steps.title: Plan
steps.body: A work breakdown with an owner on every task, a timeline built from real capacity rather than optimism, and a risk log with mitigations already assigned.

steps.title: Coordinate
steps.body: I run the cadence — standups, follow-ups, vendor chasing, approvals unblocked. Nothing sits waiting on someone remembering to send it.

steps.title: Report
steps.body: One dashboard and one weekly note: progress against plan, spend, live risks, and the decisions that need you this week. No surprises at the deadline.

engagements.heading: Pick the shape that fits the problem

tiers.title: Project engagement
tiers.body: End-to-end coordination of one defined project, from kickoff to handover. Best when you know what you're building and need someone to land it.

tiers.title: Monthly retainer
tiers.body: I act as your project coordinator across everything in flight — planning, cadence, reporting and risk — without the cost of a full-time hire.

tiers.title: Setup sprint
tiers.body: A short, intensive engagement to stand up your PMO: templates, tooling, reporting and governance, then handover to your own team.

testimonials.heading: What clients say

items.a: Yes — most engagements are fully remote, with working hours overlapping your team. I'm based in Beirut and can travel for kickoffs or key milestones where it matters.

items.q: What size of project do you take on?
items.a: Anything from a single six-week rollout to a portfolio of parallel workstreams. If a project is too small to need me, I'll tell you that in the first call.

items.q: Can you work inside our existing tools?
items.a: Almost always. I work in Jira, MS Project, Zoho, Asana, Odoo, Trello and plain spreadsheets. If your process is working, I fit into it rather than replacing it.
A 30-minute call to understand the project and the constraints, then a short written proposal: scope, cadence, deliverables and cost. No obligation on either side until that's agreed.

contact.heading: Tell me what's slipping.
contact.lead: Send a few lines about the project, the deadline and what's in the way. I'll reply within one working day with either a plan or an honest "that's not me".
contact.formNote: Sent straight to my inbox — nothing is shared.
